questions.question: What happens to the steering if your front tire goes flat while riding?

options.text: There will be no change in the steering.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes the steering feel heavy. If you notice heavy steering, pull off the road right away and check your tires.

questions.question: What should you do when someone is following you too closely?

options.text: Not worry about them and just focus on the road in front of you.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let a tailgater pass you. Speeding up makes tailgating more dangerous. Never ride on the shoulder because other drivers will not expect you there and may suddenly leave the road.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: You can see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when the road is wet because your motorcycle needs more distance to stop. Also increase it in heavy traffic or when you cannot see around the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: Occur at speeds greater than 35 mph.
Involve riders who have ridden their motorcycles for less than six months.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders who have ridden their motorcycles for less than six months.
questions.explanation: Most crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle. Be extra careful when riding a new or unfamiliar motorcycle.

questions.question: Which of these should you NOT do to improve your safety when riding at night?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight whenever possible.

questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, reduce your speed, use your high beam when not near other vehicles, and increase your following distance. Watch the headlights and taillights of vehicles ahead to help you see the road better.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake control usually located?
questions.explanation: The rear brake on a motorcycle is controlled by the right foot.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can affect a rider's ability to ride?
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can affect your ability to ride. Riding while under the influence of alcohol is both illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Which formation allows group riders to stay close together while maintaining safe space?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is the best way for a group to stay close while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file formation when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: What should riders do when changing lanes?

options.text: Rely only on their mirrors to identify other vehicles.
Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
Slam on the brakes to allow any vehicles in their blind spot to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head to check for traffic behind you before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which of these provides the best face protection for a rider?
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield or eyeglasses do not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Complete the pass without going over the speed limit.
You can finish passing in a no passing zone if you started before the zone began.
You can go faster than the speed limit.
Pass on the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Complete the pass without going over the speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must complete all passes at or below the posted speed limit. You can only pass where passing is allowed.

questions.question: Small vehicles can look ______ and seem to be going ______ than they really are.
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles can look farther away and appear to be moving slower than they actually are. This makes it hard to judge their real location and speed.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the tire that is still good.
Brake on the good tire and steer toward the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer toward the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold both handlebars firmly. Ease off the throttle and go straight. Slowly use the brake on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When you secure a load on a motorcycle, where should you place it?

options.text: On only one side of the motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Keep loads low. Placing them too high can raise the motorcycle's center of gravity and throw off its balance. Spread the load evenly on both sides of the motorcycle.

questions.question: A proper lane position helps you do all of the following, except:

options.text: See better and be seen better.

questions.explanation: Your lane position affects safety. It helps you see better and be seen, avoid blind spots, and prepare for turns. It does not help you go faster.

questions.question: To lean a motorcycle when turning, what should you do?

options.text: Press the handgrip opposite the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To turn, a motorcycle must lean. Press on the handgrip in the direction you want to turn to make the motorcycle lean that way.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. How can you lower your crash risk?

options.text: Do not ride during the day.

questions.explanation: Make yourself as visible as possible to lower crash risk. Wear bright-colored clothes when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
Trust your mirrors to show everything around you.
Point in the direction you are changing lanes.
Speed up to pass other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Mirrors alone are not enough.

questions.question: When riding in a group, motorcyclists should:

options.text: Make their space cushions half as big.
Keep enough space around each rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep enough space around each rider.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, stay close together but keep a safe space cushion around each rider.

questions.question: What is true about approved helmets?

options.text: They can block your side vision.
They let you see far to the sides as needed.
You do not have to wear one if you think it limits your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: They let you see far to the sides as needed.
questions.explanation: Some people worry that helmets limit vision, but this is not true. Approved helmets allow you to see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, where should you position yourself in the lane?

options.text: Always stay away from the left side of the lane.
Always stay away from the right side of the lane.
Always stay away from the center of the lane.
Use the safest part of the lane based on current conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the safest part of the lane based on current conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single lane position you must always avoid. Change your position based on road conditions.

questions.question: How do you brake most effectively in a straight line on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: On a straight road, use both brakes to stop in the shortest distance. Avoid locking either brake.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by the amount of alcohol consumed, how quickly it is consumed, and body weight. Height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: Where are motorcycles most likely to have conflicts with other vehicles?
questions.explanation: Intersections are where motorcycles and other vehicles are most likely to conflict. Stay alert at intersections where other vehicles may cross your path.

questions.question: What should motorcycle passengers do?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean when the operator leans. They should sit as close to the operator as possible without crowding them, and hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.
